```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(coherentSurv)
```

A robot can accumulate faults before an irrecoverable failure. Here the unit
is a robot, recurrent marks identify two fault types, and `terminal = 1`
records irreversible failure. A repair is a recurrent event only if the study
actually defines and observes it; a sensor warning is not automatically a repair.
All times below are **thousands of operating hours**. These synthetic examples
illustrate data contracts, not a deployed maintenance policy or a safety claim.

| Package quantity | Fleet interpretation |
|---|---|
| `id`, `start`, `stop` | Robot and observed operating interval |
| `event_type` | `calibration_drift`, `actuator_fault`, or `0` for no recurrence |
| `terminal` | Binary irreversible-failure indicator |
| `workload` | Baseline binary high-duty indicator |
| `risk`, `survival` | Failure probability and its complement over a stated horizon |
| `burden_*` | Expected additional fault counts, stopped at irreversible failure |
| `rmst` | Expected operating time before failure, restricted to that horizon |

Restricted operating time is not unrestricted mean time to failure, downtime,
fault-free time, or a monetary loss forecast.

## A transparent local generator

The helper delegates simulation to `cs_simulate()` rather than maintaining a
second event-history engine. For mark or failure type `k`, its intensity is
`Z * rates[k] * exp(beta[k] * workload + history[k] * H)`, where `Z` is a
mean-one gamma frailty and `H` is the **sum of the two prior mark counts, each
capped at one**. Thus failure depends on both prior fault types in this example,
not exclusively on actuator faults. There is no random censoring; observation
ends at failure or the administrative horizon.

The return value separates exact simulation traces, generating parameters, and
inspection records. The inspection table contains complete event counts and
marks but coarsens recurrence times to inspection windows. Failure is observed
immediately. It contains no hidden exact recurrence times or interval starts.

```{r simulator}
sim_robotic_fleet <- function(n = 100L, horizon = 3, inspection_width = .25,
                             seed = 2026L) {
  stopifnot(length(inspection_width) == 1L, is.finite(inspection_width),
            inspection_width > 0)
  exact <- cs_simulate(n = n, horizon = horizon,
    rates = c(.45, .25, .12), beta = c(.35, .50, .60),
    history = c(.12, .18, .22), dispersion = .35, censor_rate = 0,
    history_cap = 1L, seed = seed, time_unit = "thousand_operating_hours")
  generating_parameters <- attr(exact, "truth")
  attr(exact, "truth") <- NULL
  names(exact)[names(exact) == "x"] <- "workload"
  exact$id <- sprintf("robot-%03d", exact$id)
  labels <- c("0", "calibration_drift", "actuator_fault")
  exact$event_type <- labels[exact$event_type + 1L]
  windows <- lapply(split(exact, exact$id), function(unit) {
    end <- max(unit$stop)
    events <- unit[unit$event_type != "0" | unit$terminal == 1, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(events)) return(data.frame(id = unit$id[1],
      event_time_lower = 0, event_time_upper = 0, event_type = "0",
      terminal = 0L, followup = end, workload = unit$workload[1]))
    lower <- floor(events$stop / inspection_width) * inspection_width
    upper <- pmin(lower + inspection_width, end)
    failed <- events$terminal == 1L
    lower[failed] <- upper[failed] <- events$stop[failed]
    data.frame(id = events$id, event_time_lower = lower,
      event_time_upper = upper, event_type = events$event_type,
      terminal = events$terminal, followup = end, workload = events$workload)
  })
  observed_windows <- do.call(rbind, windows)
  rownames(observed_windows) <- NULL
  list(exact = exact, observed_windows = observed_windows,
       generating_parameters = generating_parameters)
}

fleet <- sim_robotic_fleet()
head(fleet$exact, 4)
head(fleet$observed_windows, 4)
stopifnot(!any(c("start", "stop") %in% names(fleet$observed_windows)),
          is.null(attr(fleet$observed_windows, "truth")))
```

Window endpoints are observation constraints, not successive counting-process
interval starts and stops. Unknown numbers of missing faults require a different
observation model; the window representation does not invent those events.

## Fit exact telemetry and inspect the fit

First consider an experiment with exact telemetry. We fit only the exact table.
The known simulation frailty variance is fixed at 0.35 to keep this tutorial
small; this is a declared teaching choice, not an estimator of unknown fleet
heterogeneity. History effects and workload coefficients are estimated.

```{r exact-fit}
marks <- c("calibration_drift", "actuator_fault")
trajectory <- cs_as_trajectory(fleet$exact, unit = "id",
  event_type = "event_type", event_types = marks,
  time_unit = "thousand_operating_hours")
head(cs_build_history(trajectory, cap = 1L)$counts)
fit <- cs_fit(~ workload, trajectory, event_types = marks,
  time_unit = "thousand_operating_hours",
  control = cs_control(history_cap = 1L, phi_fixed = .35),
  frailty_diagnostics = FALSE)
fit$convergence
```

An optimizer completion code does not establish regularity. Inspect the gradient,
information and boundary diagnostics before using sampling-uncertainty methods.
The examples below display point forecasts and numerical diagnostics, not
certified safety margins.

## Forecast only from an eligible robot's past

An independently seeded assessment fleet illustrates the information available
at 1,000 operating hours. Eligibility requires observation through that landmark
and no failure at or before it. We remove all later endpoints and their event
labels before passing the history to prediction. This is a prospective-history
demonstration; it reports no held-out accuracy metric.

```{r landmark-forecast}
assessment <- sim_robotic_fleet(n = 12L, seed = 2027L)$exact
assessment$id <- paste0("assessment-", assessment$id)
landmark <- 1
by_robot <- split(assessment, assessment$id)
eligible <- vapply(by_robot, function(d)
  max(d$stop) >= landmark && !any(d$terminal == 1L & d$stop <= landmark),
  logical(1))
data.frame(robot = names(eligible), eligible = unname(eligible))
chosen <- head(names(eligible)[eligible], 2L)
stopifnot(length(chosen) == 2L)
past <- assessment[assessment$id %in% chosen & assessment$start < landmark, ]
crosses_landmark <- past$stop > landmark
past$stop[crosses_landmark] <- landmark
past$event_type[crosses_landmark] <- "0"
past$terminal[crosses_landmark] <- 0L
stopifnot(all(past$stop <= landmark), all(past$terminal == 0L))
forecast <- predict(fit, past, landmark = landmark,
  horizon = c(.25, .5), type = "all", quadrature = 15L)
forecast[, c("unit", "horizon", "target", "estimate", "series_error_bound")]
probability <- forecast[forecast$target %in% c("risk", "survival"), ]
totals <- aggregate(estimate ~ unit + horizon, probability, sum)
stopifnot(max(abs(totals$estimate - 1)) < 1e-12)
```

The same retained law supplies all targets. Numerical series bounds are distinct
from uncertainty in estimated parameters, the frailty distribution and event
time integration. Compare frailty quadrature resolutions when needed:

```{r quadrature-check}
fine <- predict(fit, past, landmark = landmark,
  horizon = c(.25, .5), type = "all", quadrature = 30L)
data.frame(maximum_difference_15_vs_30 =
  max(abs(forecast$estimate - fine$estimate)))
```

This difference describes these particular forecasts; it is not a uniform
quadrature bound.

## Fit a small inspection-window experiment

The next hand-specified service-bench fixture is separate from the simulated
fleet. Eight robots have complete fault counts and follow-up through two
thousand hours or observed failure. Recurrence times are windowed, while failure
times are exact. At most two events are recorded per robot, keeping legal-path
integration small. This is an executable integration example, not an adequate
sample for validating a fleet risk model.

```{r window-fit}
inspections <- data.frame(
  id = c("bench-A", "bench-A", "bench-B", "bench-B", "bench-C", "bench-C",
         "bench-D", "bench-E", "bench-F", "bench-G", "bench-H"),
  event_time_lower = c(.2, 1.5, .4, 1.8, .1, .7, .5, 1.6, .3, 0, 0),
  event_time_upper = c(.4, 1.5, .6, 1.8, .3, .9, .7, 1.6, .5, 0, 0),
  event_type = c(marks[1], "0", marks[2], "0", marks[1], marks[2],
                 marks[2], "0", marks[1], "0", "0"),
  terminal = c(0L, 1L, 0L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L),
  followup = c(1.5, 1.5, 1.8, 1.8, 2, 2, 2, 1.6, 2, 2, 2))
window_fit <- cs_fit(~ 1, inspections, observation = "coarsened",
  event_types = marks, time_unit = "thousand_operating_hours",
  control = cs_control(history_cap = 0L, phi_fixed = .35),
  coarsening_control = list(format = "windows", nodes = 3L,
    max_perms = 8L, max_paths = 64L, draws = 64L),
  frailty_diagnostics = FALSE)
window_fit$convergence
```

This separate intercept-only working model deliberately omits history effects.
It integrates compatible histories using numerical quadrature; it does not
replace windows by midpoints or treat them as missing event counts.

For a new robot inspected through the landmark, construct a **new past-only
window table**. Do not reuse full-follow-up training fibres or future failure
records. The supplied window ends before the landmark, and `followup` equals
the landmark exactly; a straddling window would need a different observation
question and is rejected by this interface.

```{r window-forecast}
inspection_history <- data.frame(id = "new-inspected-robot",
  event_time_lower = .2, event_time_upper = .4,
  event_type = marks[1], terminal = 0L, followup = landmark)
window_forecast <- cs_predict_coarsened(window_fit, inspection_history,
  landmark = landmark, horizon = .5, type = "all", quadrature = 15L,
  coarsening_control = list(format = "windows", nodes = 3L,
    max_perms = 8L, max_paths = 64L, draws = 64L))
window_forecast[, c("unit", "target", "estimate")]
attr(window_forecast, "automatic_fibre")
stopifnot(abs(sum(window_forecast$estimate[
  window_forecast$target %in% c("risk", "survival")]) - 1) < 1e-12)
```

## A separate sensitivity model for missing whole histories

Here a hypothetical audit observes complete horizon histories for a known
fraction `rho = 0.8` of all robots. The declared support has three categories:
no failure/no fault, no failure/at least one fault, and failure. The recorded
counts below are illustrative audit counts, **not estimates from the fitted
fleet**. The recording fraction concerns whole histories, not the fraction of
individual telemetry packets or minor faults captured.

```{r recording-bounds}
counts <- c(55L, 30L, 15L)
bound <- cs_bounds(p = counts / sum(counts), numerator = c(0, 0, 1),
  kappa = 1.5, recording_fraction = .8, counts = counts)
data.frame(identification_lower = bound$lower,
  identification_upper = bound$upper,
  confidence_outer_lower = bound$outer$lower,
  confidence_outer_upper = bound$outer$upper)
random_recording <- cs_bounds(p = counts / sum(counts), numerator = c(0, 0, 1),
  kappa = 1, recording_fraction = .8)
stopifnot(abs(random_recording$lower - .15) < 1e-10,
          abs(random_recording$upper - .15) < 1e-10)
```

Identification bounds are sharp for this declared finite support and recording
model. The outer projection additionally uses multinomial sampling information.
Neither interval is a numerical-error bound or a guarantee about arbitrary
unlogged faults, an unknown recording fraction, repair effectiveness or losses.

## Retain context for review

```{r audit}
audit_json <- cs_audit_report(window_fit, predictions = window_forecast,
                              format = "json")
audit <- jsonlite::fromJSON(audit_json)
audit$convergence$code
audit$numerical$scope
```

The report records assumptions, integrity fingerprints and diagnostics. It is
mutable and unsigned; it does not certify a maintenance decision, regulatory
compliance, a clinical device or deployment safety. The local generator is a
teaching helper, not an exported package API or a calibrated engineering model.
